utterances.text: We in Dubrovnik didn't have any weapons. If you were thinking about our shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I'm not speaking in terms of "our" or "your." I'm asking you who is "we" in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about our people, our citizens who remained in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So there were no weapons at all in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, no. I didn't see any weapons, nor did I hear that -- nor did I know that there were any.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And you didn't hear that there were any weapons there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't interested, frankly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You go on in this same statement to say: "Large gunboats arrived in the area later on. I remember the name of the boats being Split and Kotor. I'm able to recall the names because I had taken a course for a unit commander and had been involved in the Croatian Civil Defence, and I have a personal interest in armaments. During my time in school, we had classes relating to the armament power of the former Yugoslavia." Can you explain to me what kind of a course for a unit commander was it you completed and this personal interest of yours in armaments.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was serving the Yugoslav People's Army as a member of a Reconnaissance Unit, in order to reconnoiter, I had to be trained. I had to know what arms I was looking for and what formations there were and existed. And as for the ships, we normally had seen them before so that at that particular point I recognised them. And then again, it was written in the newspapers what their names were. It was no secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You say that during your military service with the JNA, you completed the course for a unit commander.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it is miswritten. Actually, I was trained for lance corporal, squad leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that there is a huge difference between a squad leader who is a plain soldier and a unit commander?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We certainly do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: If nothing else, you have this necessary military experience?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to me more specifically the sentence: "During my time in school, we had classes relating to the armament power of the former Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were told --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Who? Who told you?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally my superiors who were in the Yugoslav People's Army gave us information as to the approximate power of the Yugoslav People's Army. We certainly were not given accurate information, but it was, nevertheless, quite certain that we were a quite powerful army then.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So during this training course that you attended, not for a commander of a unit but for a lance corporal, you learned all this during that time.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, where is the headquarters, the staff of the Civil Defence?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And you said that you knew Nikola Jovic.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, because we were in the same line of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was Nikola Jovic also a member of the Civil Defence?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did Nikola Jovic also perhaps on occasion leave his store in order to perform a duty for the Civil Defence?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that Nikola Jovic testified here and that he also said that he had been a member of the Civil Defence and that he had been sent on behalf of the Civil Defence to Orasac to open fire at JNA ships from a Maljutka, can you comment on that? What is your opinion about it?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what you are saying. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vlasica, I'm familiarising you with what was stated before this Tribunal by Nikola Jovic. He said that as a member of the Civil Defence --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He's asking this witness for his opinion of Nikola Jovic's testimony. I would argue that that's improper cross-examination. You're asking one witness to comment upon another witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Nikola Jovic, a witness who took the stand before this distinguished Chamber said that he had been a member of the Civil Defence, like this witness here. However, Nikola Jovic said that as a member of the Civil Defence, he had a military mission, namely to open fire from Maljutkas at the JNA ships within the framework of the same duties and obligation of a formation to which both that witness and this witness belonged. So I'm asking this witness here whether that was the -- appropriate to the Civilian Defence establishment at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, you certainly may ask him whether he was ever called on to perform any military functions, perhaps whether he knew of any other members of the Civil Defence who were called on to perform military functions, but you -- the way you were putting the question before suggested you were wanting the witness to say whether he believed or accepted what the earlier witness, Mr. Jovic, had said, and that is not a proper question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I shall rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were members of the Civil Defence, in any form, sent to perform purely military tasks?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know any other members of the Civil Defence?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As to whether I know others, I only know those people who helped other people in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vlasica, I think that helping other people in town is closely associated with the Civil Defence, but it is a personal matter of every man, of every human being. I believe that you, even if you had not been a member of the Civil Defence, would have helped people in Dubrovnik, in the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I would have, as far as that question is concerned. But we only worked within the Old City to help others, and that is what I personally know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of any member of the Civil Defence performing a military duty?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were members of the Civil Defence engaged in only assisting people in terms of providing food for the population or was there something else there too?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I was informed, this is the only thing we did. I don't know about anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you report to anyone to say that you had completed the task that had been assigned to you?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What, for instance, if it should so happen that you set out to take milk to the shelter and then you are prevented from doing that?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I took there, what supplies I did manage to take, I had to make a document about it which I then initialed and then handed it over in Dubrovnik. What happened after that, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In other words, you maintained records.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally, because I was in charge and responsible for those goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And Dubrovnik -- Dubrovkinja would then submit those records to the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was there a Crisis Staff in Dubrovnik at that time?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So you don't know anything practically. You don't know about the Crisis Staff. You don't know that there were any armaments in Dubrovnik. The only thing which you do know is that you helped people as part of your duties within the Civil Defence, taking milk to the shelter.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In the third paragraph of your statement from 2000, second sentence. In the first sentence you say: "There was severe and sporadic shelling throughout October. The JNA had actually surrounded the city of Dubrovnik during this time." Then you go on to say: "During this period, I was aware of Croatian citizens taking their speedboats and picking up small armaments from one of the islands. These armaments, including uniform and food, were being smuggled in." What is this, Mr. Vlasica?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are perfectly aware of the fact that in October there was set up a detachment of armed ships in the area of Dubrovnik. So these lads who were within this fleet of armed ships, which I only found out later, were compelled to lay their hands on as much light weaponry as they could to find a hand grenade or two in order to prevent the Yugoslav People's Army from entering the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vlasica, five minutes ago you repeated -- you decidedly repeated several times in response to my question there were no armaments in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. I think he's taking the witness out of context. At that time they were talking about the Old Town of Dubrovnik, although the question was Dubrovnik. This has been an objection I've made previous in this trial, that sometimes we refer to the Old Town as strictly Dubrovnik, sometimes you call it the Old Town, sometimes you call the whole area Dubrovnik, sometimes you refer to it as "the city" and sometimes you say "the town." If the language could be used when you're questioning about Dubrovnik, if the whole municipality, use "the municipality"; if it's strictly on the Old Town use "the Old Town," but phrases have been used on several witnesses that it becomes unclear what exactly we're speaking about. All those questions at the time were concerning the Old Town, even though the next phrase -- the next question was "Dubrovnik."

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm sorry, but I have to say my colleague is absolutely misusing his right to raise an objection and is doing something which he shouldn't be doing because up to this point you have been hearing us ask these questions. When I ask about "Dubrovnik," of course this refers to the entire city. If I'm particularly interested in the Old Town area, I underline that specifically. And people from -- of Dubrovnik who come here to testify understand this very well, whereas what my colleague is doing right now is to hint to the witness who is listening to this debate of ours, and assisting him in replying to my question when I actually pointed to the contradictory nature of his statement, and I suppose that of course now the witness shall give a reply along the lines of the Prosecutor's objection, and this is something which is really inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May I respond to that one, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, you're half right and half not right. If Mr. Weiner was doing as you suggest, you are correct, but I've got to say it has not been clear to me whether you were speaking of Dubrovnik as the municipality, the greater area, or the Old Town, and that is a confusion that I have seen has affected the evidence of more than one witness so far. So that in that respect, Mr. Weiner is well justified. I think we have drawn attention to this difficulty at this point. You may carry on with your questioning now, and we will take into account what you have said as we evaluate the evidence of the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, on page 45, line number 10, you can verify what I've just said. To my question -- to my question, "Do you have any weapons?" - and before that we had been talking about Dubrovnik - the witness decidedly said, "We in Dubrovnik did not have any weapons." So he didn't say, "We in the Old Town." He said, "We in Dubrovnik." The witness is from Dubrovnik and he knows what he is saying perfectly well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It may be clear to you, Mr. Rodic, but that was not clear to me whether he was speaking of the Old Town or of the greater municipality. You see the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the municipality of Dubrovnik is the entire city of Dubrovnik including the Old Town. The Old Town is not separate. It is just one entity within the larger entity of the municipality of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm aware of that, Mr. Rodic. I am aware of that. The point I'm making is that so much in this case depends on a distinction between the Old Town itself and the greater area which is Dubrovnik. A lot of the questioning can be understood to mean one or the other, and it's not clear at that time which is intended. The questioner may mean one thing; the answer may be intended to mean the other. So it is a matter which you need to keep in mind when you are asking questions. And when something is critical to your case, whether the witness is speaking of only the Old Town or the whole of Dubrovnik, I think you need to be careful in the way you question so that the answer is unmistakably one or the other. I've just indicated to you that an answer which you got from this witness which you referred to, to your mind was unmistakably the whole municipality. In my mind, I wasn't clear which the witness meant. I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- all counsel should watch that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will try to clarify it in the best possible way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vlasica, since you were born in Dubrovnik, grew up in Dubrovnik, spent all your time in Dubrovnik, when we say "the municipality of Dubrovnik," can you explain to us what it all includes.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipality of Dubrovnik encompasses the entire area down from Debeli Brijeg to Metkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: When we say Debeli Brijeg, that is at the border with the Republic of Montenegro, and before Debeli Brijeg there is Mokosica, Konavle and other areas that all belong to the municipality of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And when we say "the town of Dubrovnik," can you give us a more precise border of that urban area.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we say "town," we know what we mean by "town." We mean the Old Town of Dubrovnik. And when we say "Dubrovnik," then we mean a broader area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: When you say "the town of Dubrovnik," what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you. When we say "the town."

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: If you meet a German person and if he asks where you're from, do you say that you're from the Old Town or do you say that you're from Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you very nicely. As far as we down there are concerned, that is one thing. But if I were talking to a German or somebody else, I would of course say, "I come from Dubrovnik." But as far as we, the local population are concerned, we know full well what the town is, the Old Town, and what the entire town of Dubrovnik is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain to me what the town of Dubrovnik is, then.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The town of Dubrovnik is the entire area from Kantafiga to Belvedere.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The Hotel Belvedere is to the east and Kantafiga is to the west. Can you put this in a more specific context?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the town of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What goes on after Kantafiga?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sustjepan, Mokosica, et cetera, but this was the town of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And when we say "the Old Town"?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course the Old Town is within the walls, the ramparts.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, has this been clarified sufficiently now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: For this witness, yes. Whether other witnesses understand it the same way is going to be a difficult question, though. You'll have to be alert to the problem throughout the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vlasica, can we repeat this now, bearing in mind what we discussed just now? Were there any weapons and soldiers in the territory of the town of Dubrovnik in the period from October to December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the town of Dubrovnik is concerned, there were formations of the police, and there were formations of people, of course, who were defending the town of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What kind of police formations existed?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reserve police. That is as far as I know. I wasn't there, so I don't know basically.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What about this other part? Just a moment, please. This other part, when you say "people who were defending the town of Dubrovnik," tell me, please, who are these people?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are people who went of their own free will to defend our beautiful town of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So the police, both active and reserve, have been defending the town in line with their official duty, and all the rest are --

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said reserve. I did not say active police. That is number one. And as for other people who joined up, of course it was of their own free will.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vlasica, you said the reserve police, that's true. But tell me, then, what did the active police do in Dubrovnik? Were they on vacation or were they engaged?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: How come you know about the reserve police, then?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through conversations with my friends I learned that people were called up within the police force to go out and defend the town of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Who called up these people?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. They didn't tell me that. I did not go that far in my questions. I wasn't interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You do know how a reserve force operates and what the principles involved are. Did they receive call-up papers to report there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know all of this about the reserve force, and I know what you're trying to ask me, but as far as this is concerned in particular, to tell you the truth, I really don't know who called them, how they were deployed, where they were deployed. Personally, I was not in that context and I was not interested in that because I had other things to do, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What did you do from 8.00 a.m. until the end of the day?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: My friend, I was in shelters.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Which shelter?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Babin Kuk, at the house of the Karaman family. Believe me, in a room of about 20 square metres, 4 by 5 metres, there were 22 of us. And you should see what it's like, being in a room like that and waiting for a shell to hit you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In that period, did you use any other shelter?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I would go to work and if the town of Dubrovnik was being shelled very heavily, if I could not, therefore, take my car from the Old Town to Lapad, then I would seek shelter in the Old Town. Then I would not go immediately. I would leave only if I could leave, and I would stay there if I had to stay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly - and of course correct me if I'm wrong - while you were in the Old Town, you went to a shelter only if that was possible for you, that is to say if there was no danger of something hurting you between the shop and the shelter.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we would close the shop at 8.00, I would go to the shelter in Revelin or at St. John's Fort. Of course we sat there, talked about all sorts of things. We listened to the news. And when it became possible for me to leave the Old Town, when the shelling was over, then I would take my car and go to Babin Kuk, because my family was still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did that happen every day in the Old Town while you were working?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: How many times did this happen in this period between October and December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, during those two months while I worked, as far as I'm concerned and my comings and goings, I don't know exactly how many times I stayed in town, but not very many times, because from 8.00 in the morning onwards, I could go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Since this was only a few times over those two months, as you said, I would like to know what you did then between 8.00 a.m. until midnight on such days. What did you do? Did you only sit in that room at Babin Kuk?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What else? We sat there. We talked. We tried to function as best we could. There were young children there. What could we do? We couldn't take walks because we had no idea when the shelling would start. So we did not want to risk anything. We were there in the shelter, in front of the shelter. We would not move away from the house more than five metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. Now I would like to ask you to explain to me what I read out to you a short while ago, what had to do with the month of October. Namely: "I know that during this period Croatian citizens took their speedboats and picked up small arms from one of the islands. These arms, including uniforms and food, were being smuggled in." Could you elaborate on that a bit?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was a detachment of armed boats which went during the night to Kalamota and from Kalamota to Lopud, because near Dubrovnik there was a formation of armed ships of the Yugoslav People's Army. Those young men were so brave and they went there and they brought small weapons - rifles, hand grenades and things like that - because we needed that for the defence of the town of Dubrovnik. And ammunition, of course. Because we did not have anything. Had we had the weapons that were in the town of Dubrovnik until 1990 belonging to the Territorial Defence, we certainly wouldn't have needed that. But since we had nothing except for our personal weapons, hunting weapons, carbines that we ourselves had, we the citizens of the town of Dubrovnik, we gave that to the reserve force so they could use that. This was certainly needed by the defence, and that is my answer, what we went to get and what we brought.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, how do you know about this secret information and secret actions?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, quite a bit of time went by before I made my statement in 2000, and believe me, over those ten years or so, I found out quite a few things that had happened, about quite a few things that had happened, so I learnt about that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: When you say "we, the citizens for the defence," do you include yourself?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I personally was not anywhere until the 3rd of February, 2003 [sic]. I was not in any formations as far as the military is concerned, and I did not have any contact with weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, were there any Croatian troops at Babin Kuk?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I saw myself, there weren't any at Babin Kuk.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of any presence of Croatian troops at Babin Kuk?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not hear about any such thing myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What happened afterwards with these weapons and uniforms that were smuggled in on speedboats? Who was this distributed to?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I heard, this went to the front line, the defence line at Sustjepan, Srdj, and Belvedere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I just intrude to ask, were you called up for reserve service in 2003 or 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I remembered you saying that earlier, and then you answered Mr. Rodic a moment ago 2003. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am sorry. I just made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vlasica, in that period, did you move about Gruz?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because it was very dangerous.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, you said that the Zagreb Hotel is about 200 metres away from your place of residence in 1991.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What was there at the Zagreb Hotel?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps hear that the staff for the defence of the town of Dubrovnik was there, Nojko Marinovic?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you said, not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Have you heard of Nojko Marinovic?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what you heard?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that Nojko Marinovic was released from the Yugoslav People's Army, that he was a commander in Trebinje, and that he came to the Croatian side. As a person who was very knowledgeable, as far as military matters were concerned, he stood in the defence of the town of Dubrovnik, and the only thing I can say is "Thank you."

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was he in charge of the defence of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From what I heard, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What forces did he use to defend Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know. I don't know what formations he had, what size they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about Captain Cengija?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard later that Captain Cengija had been a police commander, that he was a police commander after the war ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that he was in command on Zlatni Potok and earlier at Brgat?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that I didn't hear. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you hear perhaps that the Civil Defence staff was at the Hotel Kompas?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. That's what you are saying. I really kept to myself and sought to survive, minded my own business.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is this still a military secret, Mr. Vlasica?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not a military secret. I'm telling you what I do know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about Zuljevic Aziz?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the Palma was?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I know very well. I pass by it every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the Crisis Staff of the police was there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You saw no one there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did see the reserve police there, but I don't know what they did there. It was out of my competence, was not for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: But you did see the reserve police around the Vila Palma?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see them, but it was none of my business.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were there any HOS forces in the October to December 1991 period in the town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the town of Dubrovnik, as I heard that there were HOS forces, but I didn't see them personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were there HOS members in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the Old Town, I claim and maintain that in the Old Town until the time I was wounded, I had never seen any HOS formations nor any other army within the walls of the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, where was the Territorial Defence headquarters?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know Jadranko Delas from the Secretariat for National Defence of Dubrovnik? And do you know that they used Dubrovkinja trucks, that of your firm, in other words, to bring armaments and ammunition to the port of Gruz which was then deposited between the berths number 9 and 10 in the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what you are saying. I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about it?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: When you mentioned the large-scale attack and shelling in November 1991 and the attack on the Gruz port, were there any loud explosions in the Gruz harbour?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I was at Babin Kuk, and I was observing this from the house in which I was staying. And believe you me, what I did see was really horrendous. The entire harbour was on fire. Now, whether there were explosions, whether there were things which were being kept -- whether these explosions were caused by goods being kept in the warehouses or because of the shelling, I don't know, but I do know that everything was ablaze. The coffee storehouse, the refrigeration facility, the ships; everything was on fire. Believe me, it was terrible. And also, I didn't want to stay very much outside the shelter because one never knew whether the shelling would stop -- they would stop shelling that portion and start shelling Lapad. So I didn't observe it all the time, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I believe you, but please tell me, I'm interested in whether you heard loud explosions on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that personally I don't know whether these explosions were caused by the incoming shells or, as you claim, because there were arms there and the arms exploded and caused the explosions. I couldn't tell. I couldn't distinguish between these two, so I cannot give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you see or hear that from three speedboats -- with three speedboats they were transporting people from the harbour to Ston and then were bringing back reinforcements, ammunition to town?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regard to your question whether people were taken away, I don't know. But I did hear that weapons were being brought. Whether it was being brought from Ston or Kalamota or Lopud, I don't know, because if every person knew the source of everything which was being brought in, that would have been too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know Mato from the Port Authority, from the Harbour Master's office who drove this hydrofoil?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many Matos around. Which Mato?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: He worked in the Port Authority.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please tell me his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the Vila Rasica was?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Vila Rasica? Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you see members of the ZNG there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go to the Vila Rasica. It is to the south where I was. It is on the slopes of this hill, Petka. There was no reason for me to go there, I had no business going there, so I don't know what was going on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, was the chief of the police department of Dubrovnik Djuro Korda?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that that was the commander, the head of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was a part of the Special Police Unit housed in the Old Town and a part in Srdj?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what you are saying. To the best of my knowledge, that was not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was the Croatian Party of Rights in Dubrovnik with its unit named Sokol, "Falcon," in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear about it, from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was there any kind of headquarters in the municipal assembly in the town hall next to the Rector's Palace?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what you said. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the Vila Palma is?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told you that I did, that I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: How far is it from the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps two kilometres, some two kilometres. If from Lapad station to the Old City there, three kilometres, then I believe this distance is about two kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me about the Hotel Dubrovnik President. It is at Babin Kuk; right?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were there any Croatian troops in and around that hotel?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, all the hotels at Babin Kuk were filled with civilians. There were people from Konavle, from Zupa, from the surrounding places. They were all accommodated in these hotels to fill their capacity, and the rest were accommodated in other hotels as well. What you are saying, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were there any Croatian troops in the area of Babin Kuk?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And in the area of Lapad, were there any Croatian troops there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And in the Lokrum area, the isle of Lokrum, were there any Croatian troops there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that even less, frankly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And at the Belvedere Hotel?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the Belvedere Hotel there were normally people who were defending the city. Now, whether they were in the hotel or on the surrounding slopes, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were there any troops or artillery emplacements on the Montovjerna site?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for Montovjerna and whether there were any troops there, I didn't see any personally. And as for artillery, as I told you at the beginning, we were a very poorly equipped and supplied army, so I don't see how there could have been any artillery but I don't know whether there was any.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know which part is called the Chinese wall?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a part of Montovjerna which is called the Chinese wall down there towards the stadium -- Stadion Hotel. There is a block of buildings which was built there and is called the Chinese wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were there any military positions there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I personally know, no, there weren't any military positions there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And when you look in the direction of the Old Town from the Pile Gate, to the left towards the hill, in front of the ramparts of the Old Town, were there any artillery emplacements or troops there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there may have been troops up there on the road, on the coastal highway, but as for artillery, I know that we didn't have any.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether there had been any, shall I say, makeshift bunkers, sandbags in the general area of the city of Dubrovnik? Because you moved about a lot and you could see those.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was, and this was established sometime at the end of October, I think. I cannot recall with precision. I know that we rushed to set these things up because we were expecting the forces of the Yugoslav People's Army to enter the very heart of the city, because an incredibly large number of civilians, women and children, had already set out, and we expected the Yugoslav People's Army to enter the city so that we erected these sort of bunkers for street fighting and for defence in street fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you see such a bunker, for instance, near the post office at Ilijina Glavica?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, near the post office at Ilijina Glavica there was, looking from above, or if one were expected that an army or troops would advance from above, it was normal for a bunker to be stationed properly there to stop them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was it perhaps at the Petka Hotel too?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Near the Hotel Petka? Let me try to remember. Yes, there was one. Now, I remember. There was one at the Hotel Petka as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was there one near the Boninovo health centre as well?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was one in that section as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was there one in front of the building of the electrical power authority of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one at the Lapad station, in front of the Minceta department store.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was there one near the city market?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, truth to tell, there were quite a few of them, but I do not remember the exact locations of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you remember having seen perhaps such facilities, bunkers at the Hotel Adriatic, at the Kompas Hotel, in the Lapad inlet, at Babin Kuk?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, frankly speaking, I did not move around town a lot. From where I lived, actually apart from the route which I normally took to go and to return, that was it. I didn't move about town to go about town a lot, and I cannot tell you with precision whether there were such facilities or not. Of course bunkers had been established for defence purposes. If the army were to enter the town, the Yugoslav People's Army, that is, on the next day, we of course intended to defend ourselves as best as we could, but where they were and what type of bunkers they were, I can't tell you. I can only tell you that I saw some of them en route from Babin Kuk to where I was and back as I drove my car. Later I took the other route, via Boninovo, so this is all I can tell you on the subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know Tomo Djordjevic who lives near the Elita Vila?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I hear about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will Ms. Usher please just give the witness this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Is that an exhibit or is this -- is this an exhibit? Have you got copies for --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, my learned colleague. We will see whether we will be exhibiting this, if the need arises.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vlasica, is this perhaps you on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know who this is. It doesn't look like me at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This photograph was taken some 12 or 13 years ago, in 1991.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's definitely not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Well, take the photograph in your hand and take a closer look at it.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, this is definitely not me. This couldn't be my profile, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. Please be so kind as to return the photograph to me, Ms. Usher, and I thank you.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether the Croatian army undertook any operations in the period October to December 1991 from the area of the city of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to say again that we didn't have any weaponry to speak of, and undertaking operations implies an activity involving larger scale weapons. I tell you that we only had small arms, short-barrelled arms, in fact. And now whether they undertook operations in terms of opening their own pistols or carbines towards you - and I apologise, I don't mean you, I mean the Yugoslav People's Army - I don't know that. But as for artillery, I know that there were no such operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask Ms. Usher, then, to show the witness this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So what you are saying, they just had this infantry, small arms, light arms; right?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, to the best of my knowledge and what I was able to learn was this, and this is what I say, what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Are you perhaps familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can say is that I -- that this is a mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This mortar was emplaced in Bogisica Park. Had you ever heard, did you see any mortars of the Croatian artillery there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, as for Bogisica Park, it is not en route from where I -- on the route which I took to go to and leave the Old Town. It was someplace around the medical school. What was there? I think you know better. I personally didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps hear somebody you know bragging how they were successful with just a rifle or with a mortar?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, to the extent that I was able to move about and to hear things during that period, I didn't hear anything of the kind. And being a civilian, I did not have access to anything bigger so that I didn't know if it did exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: As you were in the JNA Reconnaissance Unit during your military service period, in the Sabotage and Reconnaissance Units --

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: -- and you said that you completed a specific training course for --

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Familiarising ourselves with weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Familiarising yourselves with weaponry and that we were well trained in the equipment used by the former JNA. Were you personally interested in -- and you said that you were personally interested in armaments. Now, tell me, while moving about through Dubrovnik from your place of work in Old Town to the house in which you were accommodated, did you ever in the period October to December 1991 able to hear the sound of a mortar opening fire from that area, the Old City, the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a well-phrased question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether I heard it, yes, I certainly heard it. But whether it was fire being opened from Bogisica Park or from a section of Zarkovica, I don't know. And as I live in Lapad, the spreading of sound was something that one couldn't actually distinguish. One couldn't tell whether it was from Bogisica Park or from above the Old Town. And Zarkovica is above the city. It is only normal for these sounds to refract. So would you be able to tell whether the shooting took place from Bogisica Park or from Zarkovica? I certainly couldn't tell at that time from where the shooting came.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, is Bogisica Park towards the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Bogisica Park is on Ilijina Glavica, and it is in the direction towards the Old Town. It is not in the direction of Lapad but, rather, in that of the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And how far is it, approximately, from the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is up there near the -- passed the Hotel Imperijal and up the hill, and if you're walking on foot, perhaps 700 or 800 metres. And as the crow flies, perhaps 300 metres or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, what about Zarkovica? How far away is it, approximately, from the walls of the Old Town, the eastern walls of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, as far as Zarkovica is concerned and Bogisica Park, it's, well, around there. From St. John's Fort to Zarkovica, if we said this is 300 metres, well, it couldn't be more than 400 metres, as the crow flies, from St. John's Fort.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I won't be needing the photograph any longer now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time, Mr. Rodic? Sorry. I thought you were pausing. If you want to ask a question, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just one question in relation to this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Sir -- sir, can you just tell me -- Mr. Vlasica, can you tell me, do you know the man in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've seen him in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Just tell me, is he wearing a uniform of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can see for yourself that he's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. We can adjourn at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the record should reveal what photograph was being shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a new photograph that looks like the previous one that was already marked as an exhibit. However, during the break we'll try to make copies, and then we are going to tender it into evidence. So it has to do with the same person in Bogisica Park, which was already admitted into evidence, but now the face can be seen better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I indicate, Mr. Rodic, that it would be a significant advantage if you could complete your cross-examination this session. Just -- we leave it to you whether that is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Believe me that I will make an effort to finish today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vlasica.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we start, Your Honour, this last photograph that we had a look at, the Defence would like to tender it into evidence, and could we please have a number assigned to it? So could the usher please distribute copies to all the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we see this? It was flashed at us. There was no copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As a very special consideration as it is Friday, Mr. Weiner, you may see the exhibit, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if my learned friend doesn't realise it himself, this comes from P66. So it comes from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think Mr. Weiner has been shown a black and white copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Colour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Oh, you've got the colour, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objection. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D37.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vlasica, so during this period of time in the period between October and December 1991, did you see in the territory of the town of Dubrovnik a car or, rather, a vehicle on which a three-barrelled gun was placed, Hispano?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you see one with a mortar mounted on it?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Have you heard of any such thing?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you see a truck on which the word "Kobra" is written and there is camouflage painting on it?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you see or hear that in the area of the park of Gradac there was some Croatian artillery?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard of this; I never saw this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, was there any civilian police in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no uniforms. There wasn't any civilian police either.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was there any military police?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did it happen sometimes that Croatian soldiers would come to your store to buy something?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the Croatian army, whether they came into the Old Town, they were not allowed to enter the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And who had forbidden this?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the entrance into the Old Town, there were reserve policemen who were very strict and who did not allow any soldiers or weapons to enter the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the Old Town was a protected area, protected by UNESCO flags. And it was well known that soldiers had no business in the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So these reserve policemen, if I'm not mistaken, they were supposed to stand at the Pile Gate, at all the gates into the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are three gates leading into the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: How many reserve policemen were there at these entrances?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As many as were needed. One, two, three. I didn't count them. I just know that they did not allow anyone in. I also needed to have a pass in order to be able to get in.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So this was strictly observed?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what I claim and this is what I know very well, because I know that every time I came, I had to identify myself. I had to show identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So you never saw any uniforms in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that my answer was no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, did the siren go off or the all-alert in the area of the town of Dubrovnik, when there was shelling, of course?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how could the siren go off if there was no electricity?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You're an experienced soldier. You must have heard about things that could be done by hand. You just turn it with your hand.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard about this, but indeed I didn't see any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So there was no siren that went off in Dubrovnik in order to show that there was a state of alert and that the shelling was beginning?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You were often in the area of the Old Town, and you would certainly have heard about this if it had happened?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, why did you not go to the shelter?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I myself told you that I worked from 6.00 to 8.00, and during that time, I carried out my duties. I sold the goods that we had. If the shelling would start, of course I would not stay there. Then I would certainly go to the shelter. But after finishing my working hours, after, too, I would go there for sure, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You said that the most intensive shelling took place in November, between the 7th and 11th.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In response to my learned friend's question, you said that the port in the Old Town had been shelled and that small boats had been sunk.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were two attacks on the harbour between the 7th and the 11th of November and on the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: We are talking about the port in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you say that to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I mean when you gave the statement to them, did you tell them about that?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were you there? Did you watch the shelling, or did you see the damage due to the shelling?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, after the shelling, because believe me, I don't know who would have had the courage to go into the port area then, and all conceivable weapons were shooting at the harbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Were you badly affected by that when you saw that the old port was shelled?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had no food, and the population of the Old Town, in order to supply us with some food, they took their little boats to the area between Lokrum and the Excelsior Hotel, and they did a bit of fishing so that we would have some food because there wasn't enough food. And then their little boats were sunk. I heard that over 80 per cent of the small fishing boats were sunk during the shelling. And also the little boats that were a bit bigger.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Djelo Jusic said here before this Trial Chamber that 80 per cent of the fishing boats were destroyed in the port. Did the two of you ever discuss this particular piece of information?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not talk to Mr. Jusic about anything. That's what I heard about later, but I saw it myself when all of this was over. After the 11th, I myself went to the old port and I saw that quite a bit had been destroyed. To tell you the truth, I am not a proper assessor in order to be able to estimate the actual damage, but later on, after the first shelling and after the second shelling, people said that about 80 per cent of all these boats were destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. You said a short while ago that you told the investigators about all of this in 2000.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I did, but I said that the shelling took place between the 7th and the 12th. I said it the first time, but I don't think I referred to it specifically the second time. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vlasica, in your statement, why is there not a single letter about the shelling of the port in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, throughout the statement that I gave, I do not know whether everything can really be put together, whether everything can be put into this one or two or three hours that I had this discussion with them. Of course some things had to be omitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I asked you before, and you claimed that you read the statement more than once. And you did not notice this? You did not add this? You did not make any correction to that effect? It remained unregistered. How come now, 13 years later, you are talking about the shelling of the port and the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that some things were omitted. Some things I simply didn't mention. Also, I said to you that as for what I did say to them, that they recorded it correctly. I certainly made no mention of this particular piece of information, but I'm telling you about it now. Of course, it is only natural that I cannot remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. Let me just tell you that in the last paragraph of your statement, the one but last sentence on the first page, you say: "I remember that the worst shelling took place on the 10th. The JNA shelled the harbour of Gruz and the surrounding warehouses." How far away is the port of Gruz from the port of the Old Town? Just tell me the distance involved.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distance is four kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, yesterday before the Honourable Trial Chamber, you got up and you showed them that on the 6th of December, you were in your store, and when you heard the sound of a truck you thought that was bringing in bread, that you then stepped out with your right foot. You were at the doorstep of your store; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, I certainly did not step out. At that moment, I was not at the door. I heard the sound of the truck and I started moving towards the door. Then I walked out, and I looked left, to my left.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. And that's when you were hit by the shell or, rather, the shrapnel, when you went out then, that's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that very moment. I was standing and watching. So it wasn't that very moment, but it was a very short period of time, perhaps a minute or two. I did not go back immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, this wound of yours, when you showed it yesterday, the entry wound where your pocket is on your right thigh --

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: -- one can say that it's the upper part of the right thigh; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What about the exit wound, when you showed the inner side of your thigh? Was it at a point that was lower than the entry wound?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It went this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So the wound goes from a higher part to a lower part; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps two or three centimetres downwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the usher now to place this map before the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please use the pointer to show us your store on this map.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So at the corner of that building, the one that you pointed at?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Tell me, where did the shell fall?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said this very nicely. I don't know exactly where it fell, but I think that it fell either here on the Varteks building or this building here, Marojica Kaboga, here. One of these two places. I can't tell exactly because I never went there to see where it had actually fallen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to point to your store.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does that mean right at the corner of your building?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: The first building on the left that you showed now, the Varteks building, how far away is it from that corner?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, my door and the Varteks door are not more than seven or eight metres apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Can you describe this building to me? Please point at the Varteks building with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Please describe the building. What's in there?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Downstairs is the Varteks ready-made clothing boutique. Further up was the restaurant of the Dubravka Hotel, the terrace of the restaurant of the Dubravka Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: This terrace of the restaurant is upstairs, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's a bridge here from this building to the terrace, and the street is not this wide; it's a very small street.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: How high up is this terrace of the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three or four metres. Three metres, three or four.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Does it have a stone edge?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go there, but I think you can only sit there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: How high is this little stone wall?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's about as tall as the armchair I'm sitting in.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: About a metre?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, less.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you said: "The shell exploded on the terrace of the restaurant that is around the corner from the store. Since the streets in the Old Town are very narrow, the shrapnel from this shell ricochetted back and forth between the walls and struck me." So behind the corner there was a restaurant?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, round the corner. If you look at the Hotel Dubravka. Of course this is around the corner. I mean, please don't split hairs in terms of every little word I say. It fell nearby, so of course it was not far away. If you look at it, it's only a few metres. It can't be more than ten metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And the height is about three or four metres?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And there is this small wall around the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no wall. That's where people sit. It's not a wall. It's like stone benches, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. So you stepped out with your right foot, and you were then hit by this shrapnel; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you fall after you were hit?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I turned around and I said, "Kate, I was hit." I entered the shop and walked for about two metres and then I lay on the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What were you wearing that day?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was wearing jeans. I had boots that we call Canadian boots, and I had jeans trousers on, and up, I had a lined jeans jacket, a padded one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Why did you say yesterday that this piece of shrapnel hit you in the right foot?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that. I said in the right upper leg.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: It says the right foot in the transcript. Perhaps it was mistranslated.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said in the right upper leg. I can show it to you personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: All right. And in your statement, you say: "A large piece of shrapnel passed directly through my right upper leg and many smaller pieces hit my feet and arms. I only received bruises from these since I had been wearing boots and a jacket." Is that so?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: What kinds of bruises were these? Were these scratches? Were these bleeding wounds; what?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These were minor bruises because the shrapnel pieces had already lost in impetus by the time they reached me because they had already hit the walls. In fact, I found a piece of shrapnel in the pocket of my jacket, and one had hit me just above the boot, in the shin, and some in the arms, but that was minor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So you also found that piece of shrapnel in your pocket?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a very tiny piece of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And was your jacket, your parka, was it green?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is a jean jacket, which is a windbreaker. It was blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And what kind of clothes was Tonci Skocko wearing?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in civilian clothing, and what exactly he was wearing, I don't know. I know those were civilian clothes. He was normally dressed like myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: You don't remember a single item of his clothing? Was he also wearing jeans?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you frankly, I cannot remember with precision. I just saw this in a jiffy. This was all a very brief time and I had only a few moments in which to see him. He didn't stop at the door at all. It was just a matter of seconds, but I saw him well. I did see what he was wearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Why didn't you make a single reference in your statement to the investigator to either the fact that you had seen Tonci Skocko nor that you knew that Tonci Skocko had been killed nor that you knew that a piece of shrapnel had pierced his heart, as you stated? Why didn't you mention this by a single word in your 2000 statement?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told what they asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Was this not an important piece of information for you to give them?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you frankly, had they had asked me, I would have told them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: And if they didn't ask you, you wouldn't?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why would I?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Isn't Tonci Skocko more important than some little boat in the port?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You're asking this witness to speculate as to the questions that the investigators should or should not have asked him. He can't answer that, why they didn't ask him, if they considered it important, if he considers it important. It wasn't asked of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it's clear, Mr. Rodic, that this matter was not mentioned to be included in the statement. We've noted that, but it is now given in evidence. We've appreciated the distinction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that at your store you lay bleeding for over two hours and a half and that the advice of the doctor to your colleague Kate Buric was to keep you awake and not let you fall asleep; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Is it not the case that, due to blood loss, immediately after you left the Old Town you fainted?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was at the Pile Gate that I lost consciousness. I cannot remember the route.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: We heard that. Let's move on, please. Would you be so kind as to position this map so that you are able to show us on the screen which route you took in your car and to tell us how much time it took you to get out of the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the shop is here, when he came with his car, the yellow Golf here, we took the Od Puca Street directly this way, up to this fountain here, and then we exited on Pile.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So how much time, approximately, did it take you from the store to reach the Pile Gate? How much time was that, roughly?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, seeing what the situation was at that time, I'm quite sure that he speeded, but he couldn't have sped so much because of all the material that had fallen from the roofs and was obstructing our -- the street. So I cannot tell you exactly how much time it took us to get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Did you enter the car yourself or did someone carry you in?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He carried me into the vehicle. I was already very, very weak and couldn't get inside myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Where did he put you, in the front or in the back?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He put me in the front seat which he had reclined, and of course he lay me on this reclining seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: So you were actually lying in the car?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was. And that is why I could see. As I lay there, I could see these buildings ablaze and on fire to my left.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, so you assert that in such a condition, wounded, losing much blood soon after -- and soon after you left the Old Town you had also fainted, you were nevertheless speeding through the Old Town in order to save your life, and you managed to register all the damage that you indicated in response to the Prosecutor's questions; is that so?

utterances.speaker: IVO VLASICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I was not bleeding any more because the blood loss had been staunched. And secondly, I'm quite sure and I claim that I saw what I saw in terms of damage. I didn't see the actual damage on the external walls in terms of how much of damage there was. What I did see was that I -- were houses burning. It was only two months later when I returned to the Old Town that I saw what we had lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
